OPENED (file read, not in diff): `src/billing/subscriptions.ts` — `handleChangePlan` already treats `executePlanChange`'s `{success:false, error, preview}` as a 402 response, so the new "suspend not confirmed -> change nothing" return path (added in `plan-change.ts`) is handled by its only caller without further changes. The new `previewPlanChange` throw on an unknown-tier plan propagates to a 400 via the route's existing global error handling (confirmed via `search_code` hit on `src/index.ts` for the `status: 400` pattern) — matches the PR's claim.

RED-FIRST: independently fetched commit c94dce50 (parent of the fix commit) — it touches only `src/__tests__/plan-change-downgrade.test.ts` (+343) and an 11-line stub `pending-plan-change.ts`, zero lines in `plan-change.ts`/`webhooks.ts`/`queries.ts`/`index.ts`. So the claimed "9 failed | 3 passed (12)" at that sha is testing the real unfixed defect, not a fixture. All 12 tests in the new file are genuine red-first (tier order for 'pro' both directions, unknown-plan refusal, scheduling with suspend-failure rollback, webhook suppression of our own suspension, upgrade clearing a pending downgrade, the daily-apply charge/new-plan/cancel-old flow, not-yet-due no-op, claim race/idempotency, declined-card retry, yearly no-charge switch).

PREMISE: the Issue Diagnostician flagged occurrence as UNMEASURED and named the exact D1 query needed. The PR's "Prod measurement (read-only, 2026-10-22)" answers it directly: 0 subscriptions currently hold a pendingPlanChange, 1 live pro subscription exists. That also satisfies the issue's backfill step (nothing to backfill right now).

BLAST RADIUS: all four `clearPendingPlanChange` call sites added to `plan-change.ts` are purely additive (free-downgrade, yearly-upgrade, monthly-upgrade branches untouched otherwise); `PLAN_ORDER` renumbering (team 2, pro 3, scale 3, business 4, enterprise 5) preserves every existing relative order, it only inserts 'pro' at its correct price tier between team and business. The webhook suppression is scoped to subscriptions that actually hold a pendingPlanChange, not a blanket bypass of suspension handling. `reconcileBillingGaps` and the operator `reactivate-plan` route are untouched, as required.

CLOSES: commit ada4230f ends "Closes #98". The commit fixes the full mechanism (PLAN_ORDER gap, the never-read pendingPlanChange, the failed-suspend-still-proceeding bug, and the webhook echo). The issue's step 4 (sprigr-team's `validPlans`/apply-at-effective-date companion) is explicitly called out by the Issue Diagnostician as its own possible sprigr-team issue, and the PR body states it out of scope — consistent with "Closes" rather than "Refs" for this repo's issue.

Minimal scope: 6 files, all load-bearing to the fix; no drive-by changes found.

VERDICT: APPROVE | Fixes #98 end to end (tier gap + scheduled downgrade + webhook echo), red-first-proven tests (12/12, independently confirmed red at the pre-fix commit), CI green, prod premise measured, blast radius additive and contained to the downgrade/pro-tier paths.

Reviewed sprigr-platform#157 for sprigr-team#12660, delta d1608e3...703bf4c (1 new commit, 2 files, +57/-1) since my prior REQUEST_CHANGES on d1608e3. CI green (coauthor-attribution + typecheck, 703bf4c). Earlier commit (d1608e3) stands on its own prior verdict; this review covers only the delta.

- The delta wraps the `remindMissingCard` call inside `giveBack` in its own try/catch (log + continue, no rethrow) — exactly the fix I asked for, confirmed by diffing `pending-plan-change.ts` between the two commits directly: the call was bare in d1608e3, now caught in 703bf4c.

- RED-FIRST, traced by hand: the new "a reminder email failure on one no-card downgrade does not abort the cron tick for the others" test mocks SES to 500 for every send and seeds two due no-card subscriptions. Against unfixed d1608e3 (bare call), `sendPaymentMethodReminderEmail`'s throw propagates out of `giveBack` and the whole `applyDuePendingPlanChanges()` call rejects after the first row, so `sub_nocard_b` is never visited — the test's `expect(summary).toMatchObject({applied:0,failed:2})` and the attempts:1 assertion on row B genuinely fail pre-fix. Against 703bf4c it passes, matching the fix exactly.
- The pattern mirrors `reconcileBillingGaps` (plan-backfill.ts) as claimed: independently confirmed its reminder loop uses `try { ... } catch (err) { summary.errors++; console.error(...) }` per customer, same shape as the new `giveBack` guard.
- Scope: 2 files, narrowly targeted at the one unguarded call I named; no other blast radius.
- Note (non-blocking): the new commit's message says "Closes #12660" rather than "Refs sprigr/sprigr-team#12660" like the first commit, which contradicts the PR body's own stated policy ("a partial fix against a multi-option diagnosis gets Refs, not Closes" — fix class b is unchanged by this delta). Practically inert here (sprigr-platform has no local issue #12660 — confirmed 404 — and this merges to staging, not main, so the keyword would not auto-close anything), but worth squashing to "Refs sprigr/sprigr-team#12660" before merge for a clean git history.

VERDICT: APPROVE | delta d1608e3...703bf4c correctly wraps the previously-unguarded remindMissingCard call in try/catch, mirroring reconcileBillingGaps's existing pattern; new test is genuinely red-first against the unfixed call and green after. Minor non-blocking note on the new commit's closing keyword above.

[tech-lead-reviewer] **Consult answer, NOT a new verdict.** My APPROVE on this head stands unchanged (`5429141427`, `<!-- verdict sha=37bd972 -->`). Nothing is re-reviewed here. But **its one merge condition is now definitively UNMET, and this is not a flake — do not merge.**

## `pr-typecheck` is failing correctly, and this PR caused it

I read the job log (run `32997281513`, job `98269734341`). The failing step is **`Enforce test-file typecheck ratchet`**, and it names this PR explicitly:

```
[test-typecheck-ratchet] FAIL: test files gained type errors.
  workers/agent: 204 error(s), manifest allows 203
    __tests__/workflow-step-runner.test.ts (2)  <-- CHANGED BY THIS PR, start here
```

**Exactly one net-new error, and I pinned which of the two it is.** I diffed the file against the ratchet base `3288f879`:

- `:60` (`TS2322` on the `deps` literal) is **byte-identical in the base** — pre-existing, grandfathered inside the 203.
- **`:294` is yours.** `expect(deps.toolContext.inboundSource).toBeUndefined();` is a line your new test added; the base file contains no `deps.toolContext.` property access at all. `WorkflowStepRunnerDeps.toolContext` is typed `ToolContext | null`, so the unguarded access is `TS18047: 'deps.toolContext' is possibly 'null'`. That is the `203 → 204`.

## Why your local run and CI do not actually disagree

**They agree — you ran a different check.** `pnpm turbo typecheck` compiles each package's `tsc --noEmit`, which does not include `__tests__/`. The CI log shows that same step passing right above the failure: `Tasks: 45 successful, 45 total` — **your exact 45/45**. The ratchet then runs `scripts/ci/check-test-typecheck-ratchet.mts`, which probes test files through a separate `tsconfig.test-ratchet-probe.json`. Your 45/45 was real and so is the failure; the gate you skipped is the one that covers test files. Run `node scripts/ci/check-test-typecheck-ratchet.mts` locally before the next push.

## The fix

**Delete line 294.** It is redundant, not just untyped: `:293` already asserts `expect(toolContext.inboundSource).toBeUndefined()` on **the same object** — `makeRunner` passes that very `toolContext` in as `deps.toolContext` (`:58`, `:64`), and the local `const` is non-null-typed. You lose no coverage. If you would rather keep the second assertion explicit, `deps.toolContext?.inboundSource` also satisfies the checker.

**Do not raise the manifest** — the ratchet's own failure text says it only ratchets down.

One-line test-only change; push it and my re-review is cheap. The substantive fix (the scoped-clone stamp) is unaffected and still approved.
